attributes.residual: The rule stays. THE MECHANISM, from the aligned raw view: the function runs the same four-iteration Newton-Raphson reciprocal-square-root kernel twice - once unguarded for the flyby camera (0x84-0xd0) and once inside the `bdnz` player loop (0x168-0x1ac) - and the whole 42-word gap is which volatile FPRs carry the squared distance and the two f64 refinement constants. In the FIRST kernel our constants already agree with retail (`sNewtonThree` in f2 in both) and only the distance register differs, target f5 against ours f4. In the SECOND kernel the loop-invariant constants are hoisted before the loop and take target f3/f2 against our f5/f4, with the distance at target f3 against our f3-versus-f5 pairing, cascading through every fmul/fnmsub in the arm. The callee-saved accumulator is f31 in BOTH streams and agrees at `@0x1bc fcmpo cr0,fX,f31` and `@0x1c4 fmr f31,fX`, which is the sharp contrast with fn_80051480, where the accumulator placement WAS the whole residual. Here the accumulator is already right and only the volatile numbering around the hoisted constants is wrong.

hypothesis.statement: This is the third measured member of one family (see claim.law.PR_the-rsqrt-newton-kernel-volatile-fpr-permutation-is-one-family.20260903.v1), and the family's untried lever is the CONSTANT HOIST, not the accumulator: retail hoists `sArrowFloorYOffset` and `sNewtonThree` into f3/f2 before the loop while ours hoists them into f5/f4, and the distance register numbering follows from what is left.
